text: [3:446] “Intentional injury” exclusion: CGL bodily injury coverage may also be excluded because the victim's injuries are deemed “expected or intended by the insured” (see ¶ 3:311). d. [3:447] Ins.C. § 533 may bar indemnity coverage: Moreover, sexual harassment is clearly a willfully-caused injury within the meaning of Ins.C. § 533, which operates as an implied exclusion in every insurance policy (see ¶ 3:105 ff.). One court has stated that section 533 precludes coverage in a sexual harassment case because sexual harassment “is always intentional, it is always wrongful, and it is always harmful.” [Coit Drapery Cleaners, Inc. v. Sequoia Ins. Co. (1993) 14 CA4th 1595, 1614, 18 CR2d 692, 705 (emphasis in original; quoting J.C. Penney Cas. Ins. Co. v. M.K. (1991) 52 C3d 1009, 1025, 278 CR 64, 73 (addressing coverage for child molestation); internal quotes omitted); but see Markel American 8 Ins. Co. v. G.L. Anderson Ins. Services, Inc. (ED CA 2010) 715 F.Supp.2d 1068, 1077-1078 (applying Calif. law)—sexual harassment claim does not necessarily implicate intentional or willful conduct] [3:448] Reserved.
